analysis: Cross-source read: the morning is a tug-of-war between the AI-capex inquest and the AI-demand bid. Burry's write-off warning is no longer a single headline: the detail now circulating (MSFT's $300B+ uncommenced leases and 15-to-25-year life extension, AMZN's doubled long-term debt, META's ~$700B and GOOGL's ~$900B in off-balance-sheet commitments) keeps the accounting-scrutiny pressure on the hyperscalers, and Oracle's force majeure on a New Mexico data center adds an execution-stumble datapoint to the same debate. On the other side, Musk's overnight Colossus numbers (~780K NVDA chips live, up to ~1.44M this year) are a hard demand datapoint, and the AKAM bid (+19.8%) plus +2% across AMD/MRVL/Cerebras/INTC shows the AI bid is still the tape's engine. Rates remain the ceiling: October-hike odds sit ~75-77%, the 10Y is 5.176% off Thursday's 5.15-5.21% highs, and the August durable goods print (due 8:30 AM ET, consensus -0.3%) could re-tax or relieve the long end depending on how hot it runs. What changed vs the 5 AM brief: Costco's Q4 detail is now in (beat, but tariff-refund-fueled with slowing membership growth, shares flat); the Burry numbers got specific; Oracle's force majeure is new carried context; October odds ticked down slightly to ~75-77%; and the durable goods print is now past due with no confirmed number in sourced pages. Signal vs noise: futures levels, the 10Y, Costco's reported figures, Burry's own published figures, the Oracle force majeure (two outlets), the Colossus numbers, and the AKAM bid are confirmed across outlets; the durable goods print, Goldman-underweight, and China EV-export 33% items are single-source or unconfirmed, treat as fragile.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures firmed into the final 30 minutes before the open: S&P 500 futures +0.38%, Dow futures +0.36% (Barron's), Nasdaq 100 futures +0.7% (Investopedia). The 10Y sat at 5.176%, off Thursday's 5.15-5.21% highs; Brent crude -2.02% (~$93); gold futures +1.14% to ~$4,347; BTC $84,912 (+0.63%).
headlines.why_it_matters: Yields and oil cooling overnight eases the squeeze on multiples into the open, but the bid is still narrow: AI hardware names plus lower yields, not broad participation, against a 75-77% October-hike print.

headlines.headline: The Census Bureau's August advance durable goods report was due at 8:30 AM ET (WSJ/Dow Jones consensus -0.3%, prior +1.1%). No confirmed print had surfaced in sourced pages by brief time; single-source relays conflict, so no number is reported here.
headlines.why_it_matters: The one hard-data event of the morning: a hot print feeds the 'economy can handle hikes' case and re-pressures the long end; a soft one relieves yields. Treat any pre-open number circulating as fragile until confirmed.

headlines.headline: Fed funds futures priced ~75.3% odds of an October 28 hike and ~58.6% for December (tradingnews), a touch below the ~77.5% October print from Thursday. Williams called another 2026 hike 'reasonable' without committing to October; Philly's Paulson said 'some modest further tightening may be warranted.'
headlines.why_it_matters: The market is still pricing a probability, not a plan, so the ceiling on growth multiples stays in place into every data point; Guha's 'expectations trap' framing is why green futures and hawkish odds coexist.

headlines.headline: Costco beat on Q4: revenue $95.72B vs $94.86B est, EPS $6.75 vs $6.54 est (Reuters, Morningstar). But $0.15/share came from one-off IEEPA tariff refunds, and membership-fee income growth slowed to 7.3%, the third straight quarterly deceleration. Shares were flat after hours.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat that reads as quality-discounted: the refund flatters the EPS line and the membership slowdown is the metric that underpins the model, which is why the stock didn't move on the headline beat.

headlines.headline: Burry's AI-capex warning gained specifics: MSFT's uncommenced leases nearly tripled to over $300B while it extended data-center useful life from 15 to 25 years; AMZN's uncommenced leases/purchase commitments surged 81% to ~$267B with long-term debt doubling to $128.9B; META carries ~$700B in uncommenced leases/purchase obligations, GOOGL nearly $900B in off-balance-sheet commitments (Stocktwits summary of Burry's note).
headlines.why_it_matters: Turns a narrative warning into auditable balance-sheet line items for the four biggest hyperscalers, which is why the overbuild/write-off debate keeps resurfacing on the tape even on green mornings.

headlines.headline: Oracle fell 3.5% Thursday after declaring force majeure over setbacks to a data center development in New Mexico (tradingeconomics Thursday recap; also flagged by Barron's). Thursday's hyperscalers were mixed: GOOGL +1.3%, META +4.5%, MSFT -0.5%, AMZN flat.
headlines.why_it_matters: An execution stumble in the AI buildout lands the same week the tape is debating whether the buildout is overdone, adding a third front (execution) to the equity and credit angles of the capex story.

headlines.headline: Musk's overnight Colossus numbers stand: ~780,000 Nvidia chips live across Hopper and Blackwell generations, another 220,000 GB300s next week and 220k more in October, potentially ~1.44M total this year. NVDA was marginally higher in premarket; chip stocks AMD, Marvell, Cerebras and Intel were each +2% (Reuters).
headlines.why_it_matters: A concrete customer-level demand datapoint for NVDA hardware and the broader chip complex, pushing back on the overbuild narrative the same morning Burry's write-off warning deepens.

headlines.headline: Akamai held its bid at +19.8% premarket on the $11.6B Anthropic cloud deal (Barron's); Corteva +5.7% led non-AI gainers. Meta traded flat, on track for a fifth straight weekly gain and less than 1% from a $2T market cap on Muse/Charm traction (Reuters). Tesla was marginally higher.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI bid is still the tape's engine: one confirmed mega-deal plus consumer-AI traction is doing the lifting while the rest of the market waits on rates and oil.

headlines.headline: A report that US and Iranian negotiators are exploring a phased path out of the war, with Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade (Reuters), helped pull oil lower after Thursday's 3%+ spike on a Houthi missile attack on Saudi Arabia.
headlines.why_it_matters: The single biggest swing factor for inflation expectations this week: real progress toward Hormuz flows would unwind the energy-risk premium that has been taxing yields and multiples.

headlines.headline: China's EV exports jumped 33% year over year, with a significant increase in exports to Europe and other markets (Seeking Alpha relay).
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source relay, unconfirmed, treat as fragile; sustained export growth from Chinese automakers is the standing margin-and-share pressure story for Tesla outside the US.

market_snapshot.breadth_notes: Prior regular session (Thu): Dow -162 pts (-0.31%) to 51,350, third straight down day; S&P 500 -0.02%; Nasdaq roughly flat. NYSE decliners beat advancers ~2:1 (Investor's Business Daily). 10Y topped 5.15% (2007 highs) before easing; 30Y hit its highest since 2004; oil +3%+ Thursday on Houthi missile attack on Saudi Arabia, then eased on Hormuz-talks report. Premarket Fri: S&P futures +0.38%, Dow +0.36% (Barron's), Nasdaq 100 +0.7% (Investopedia); 10Y 5.176%; VIX futures +1.47%; Brent -2.02% (~$93); gold futures +1.14% to ~$4,347; BTC $84,912 (+0.63%); Nikkei +1.30%, STOXX Europe 600 +0.65%. Weekly: S&P and Nasdaq set for second straight weekly gains, Dow -0.6%. Dollar set for first back-to-back weekly gains in 3+ months (DXY ~101.2, devdiscourse); mortgage rates topped 7% for the first time in over a year (Investopedia).
market_snapshot.notes: 30 minutes before the open: the AI bid (AKAM +19.8%, chips +2%, NVDA on Colossus numbers) carries the morning against a ~75-77% October-hike print and a 5.176% 10Y. Yields and oil cooled overnight on the Hormuz-talks report. The 8:30 AM ET August durable goods print had no confirmed number in sourced pages by brief time.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight; carried context stands: the Sept 9/10 $600M 6.75% senior notes pricing (due 2035, net ~$592M to repay credit borrowings) and the NYSE-to-TXSE listing transfer (NYSE trading ends Oct 2, TXSE begins Oct 5, ticker unchanged). Q2 recap: revenue $342.1M, adjusted EBITDA $193.2M, DCF coverage 1.65x, $0.525 distribution, full-year guidance confirmed (EBITDA $770-800M, DCF $480-510M). Units open into a slightly softer oil tape (Brent -2% premarket), a modest sector tailwind for the Friday session.

watch_next: The 8:30 AM ET August durable goods print: watch the tape for a confirmed number (consensus -0.3%, prior +1.1%) and the yield reaction; a hot print re-taxes the long end, a soft one relieves it.
10:00 AM ET: Michigan consumer sentiment final (WSJ/Dow Jones consensus 47.8, prelim 47.8).
Fedspeak: Schmid at 9:20 AM ET, Hammack at 2 PM ET; watch for any October-commitment language that moves the ~75-77% odds.
At the open: does the AKAM bid hold, and does the Burry write-off narrative fade against Musk's Colossus numbers and the chip bid; 10Y vs Thursday's 5.15-5.21% highs.
China EV-export 33% figure: watch for Tesla or trade outlets confirming or contesting the number.
